title: PIREUS continuity proposal wire format
purpose: State, executably, the language that admission.sio's hand-written parser accepts, and specify the minimal extension a kind=2 operator proposal requires.
why_this_exists: The accepted language is entirely implicit in the parser's control flow. Nothing states it, so nothing can validate a proposal before the engine refuses it, nothing pins the language against drift, and anyone extending it works from prose. eisa_h.pireus_operator_admission.v1 leaves the .sio admission path open; this contract makes that change mechanical by pinning what the change has to preserve before anyone writes it.

provenance.why_not: This environment cannot build bin/souc: gen2 self-compilation measured 27,294,756 KiB maximum child RSS on Slurm job 11991 and the container has 15 GiB. The v1 rules are therefore a claim about admission.sio that a compiler owner must confirm, not a measurement of it.
provenance.how_to_confirm: Every rule carries the admission.sio line it came from, so confirmation is a reading task rather than an investigation.
provenance.authority: admission.sio is the authority. A disagreement between it and this contract is a defect in this contract until proven otherwise.

language.shape: A single JSON object. Whitespace (space, tab, LF, CR) is skipped around structural tokens only. admission.sio:32.
language.keys: Lowercase ASCII letters and underscore only; no key outside the table; no duplicates. admission.sio:52, :71.
language.values: Nonnegative decimal integers of at most nine digits with no leading zero, except the context key, which is a quoted string of exactly 64 lowercase hex characters. There is no sign, no float, no negative. admission.sio:78-102.
language.termination: The object must close immediately after a key-value pair, and only whitespace may follow the closing brace. admission.sio:106-112.
language.bounds: The document is 1..4096 bytes and byte-indexed, so any multi-byte character breaks the parser's length invariant. admission.sio:40, :170.
language.one_encoding_per_value: Leading zeros and uppercase hex are both refused, so each admissible value has exactly one wire encoding. That is what makes the proposal digest meaningful.

extension.principle: One key, no other change to the language. A kind=2 proposal is a kind=1 proposal plus the 16-bit phase code that names the operator; every other field keeps its meaning, and the lane plan still applies because a proposed operator still has to be lowered.
extension.why_a_17th_key_fails_today: Not because the name is unknown. The parser loop is bounded at 16 pairs and sets valid only when the object closes inside the loop, so a 17-key document falls out of the loop and returns invalid. Extending the language therefore means raising the bound, not only adding a name.
required_edits: admission.sio:60 key lookup: `while k < 16` becomes `while k < 17`.
admission.sio:176 proposal mask: accept 65087 for kind=1 and 130623 for kind=2, and no other value.
admission.sio:188 kind gate: `if p.values[9] != 1` becomes a branch on kind 1 or 2, refusing everything else, and binding the mask to the kind so a phase key cannot ride along on a kind=1 proposal.

admission.sio:213-246 tensor reconstruction: for kind=2, reconstruct against the twisted product sigma_B rather than cd_sigma, where B is values[16]. The discipline is unchanged -- the engine computes the tensor, the proposer names only B.

admission.sio:247-250 materialisation guard: refuse for kind != 1. emit_lowering_ptx encodes the Cayley-Dickson signs and takes no phase argument, so for kind=2 it would emit the wrong operator silently.

admission.sio:251-258 receipt emitter: a kind=2 receipt carries the phase code and reports novelty NOT_CLASSIFIED, naming eisa_h.pireus_operator_atlas.v1 as the classifier. admission.sio cannot decide novelty: that needs the GL(4,2) atlas, which does not belong in a bounded executable reading a 4096-byte document.
extension.no_struct_change_needed: Document already declares `values: [i64; 18]` (admission.sio:9), so index 16 is free and the seen bitmask has room. The 4096-byte bound also holds: one more key costs at most 14 bytes.
extension.not_in_scope: This contract states what the edits must preserve. The patch that makes them lives in patches/sounio/ and has not been compiled or executed.
extension.edit_count_correction: This list said six until the patch was actually written. Building it revealed two more: the materialisation guard and the receipt emitter. The guard is the more serious omission -- a patch following the six-edit list would have left emit_lowering_ptx emitting Cayley-Dickson PTX for a twisted operator, silently and with a green admission receipt. Corrected here rather than left standing; the patch itself is verified against the corrected list by eisa_h.pireus_admission_patch.v1.

invariants.wire_and_admission_are_separate_obligati: A well-formed kind=2 document with phase code 0 is accepted by this contract and refused by eisa_h.pireus_operator_admission.v1 for lacking novelty. Conflating the two would let a parser decide a semantic question.
invariants.mask_is_exact: A proposal carries fields 0..5 and 9..15, plus 16 when kind=2. Fields 6, 7 and 8 are context-only; a proposal that sets its own capabilities, lane width or facts state is refused.

claim_boundary.note: This validates documents against a described language. It does not prove the description matches the engine -- that needs a compiler owner, or a host that can build souc -- and it decides nothing about whether a well-formed proposal should be admitted.
